No anti-adblock detector or wall is involved:⁠ the page renders its content behind the overlay and no detector script appears in the captured requests. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — jpopsingles.eu serves an inline "AdBlock Detected" detector that builds a randomized-id full-screen overlay, locks scrolling and breaks right-click, and none of the site's existing anti-adblock rules stops it. Three candidate rules (two scriptlets and one HTML-filtering rule) produced no change in any experiment phase while the experiment's own probe reported no anti-adblock detected and no applied rules, so no candidate could be verified and the best scriptlet candidate is handed over for human review.

## Candidate for review

`jpopsingles.eu#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-stack-trace', 'requestAnimationFrame', 'js_func_frame_loop')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: All three experiments came back environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with empty failedCandidateChecks, and the vision review rejected each as 'symptom:⁠ not_resolved' with pageIntegrity intact and no observedDamage. The record contradicts what it captured:⁠ phase A reported an empty appliedRules list although the run's own session lists 21 applied rules on the same page, phase C reported antiAdblockDetected:⁠false although that phase's screenshots show the banner, and two candidates produced byte-identical before/after full-page captures. That points to the candidate not being applied by the adapter's filtering engine rather than to a proven failure of the rule, so it stayed browser-unverified. The mechanism it targets is evidenced separately:⁠ only the detector's inline script uses requestAnimationFrame on this page, and js_func_frame_loop stayed stable across two loads while all other identifiers were randomized.

## Still visible after the rule

- Top center above the post grid, overlapping site header/navigation and first post cards — Visible anti-adblock overlay:⁠ red 'AdBlock Detected' header with white message box 'Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us.' over a dark translucent blackout layer. The site logo, navigation, first post cards ([⁠Single]⁠ PIGMONZ – G.M.B.A and [⁠Single]⁠ ZARAME – Kodou), sidebar Info/Donate area, and Recent Posts are dimmed behind it.
- Top center, overlapping the site header/navigation above the post grid — Prominent anti-adblock banner:⁠ red header reads "AdBlock Detected" and a white box reads "Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us."; the reporter circled this banner in red.
- Full page behind the banner, including header, navigation, post cards and right sidebar — Dark blackout/dim overlay covers the page content beneath the anti-adblock banner, matching the gated/dimmed page state described by the reporter.

## Missing information

- Scriptlet argument semantics (abort-on-stack-trace / abort-current-inline-script) and HTML-filtering support in AdGuard CLI are not covered by the run's guidance documents: The run's three linked documents (create-own-filters.md, filter-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) served via lookup_rule_guidance give the #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet rule syntax and the $$ HTML-filtering syntax with :⁠contains(), but not the per-scriptlet argument semantics of the Scriptlets library (what abort-current-inline-script's property/searchString actually match against, and what abort-on-stack-trace matches in a stack frame), nor which of scriptlets/HTML filtering the AdGuard CLI adapter actually applies. I needed both:⁠ the candidate had to abort an inline detector that only touches the trapped property from inside a load-event callback, and no document states whether HTML filtering rules are executed by the CLI product or by the experiment adapter.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZW0tKX_iFhc&t=109s](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DZW0tKX_iFhc%26t%3D109s) ### Comment > ## Summary > > YouTube AI auto-dubbed audio tracks disappear when AdGuard for Windows filters HTTPS traffic for `youtube.com`. Adding only `youtube.com` to the HTTPS allowlist brings them back. No filtering rule seems to be involved. > > ## Screenshots (UI is in Portuguese, translation below) > > Both screenshots show the same video, in the same browser, a few seconds apart. The only change is the AdGuard protection toggle. > > **Screenshot 1 - AdGuard ON (dubbing missing)** > > - AdGuard window: "A protecao esta ativada" = "Protection is enabled" > - YouTube player settings menu: > - Volume estavel = Stable volume: **available, ON** > - Iluminacao cinematografica = Ambient mode: ON > - **Faixa de audio = Audio track: MISSING** > - Legendas/CC = Subtitles/CC: Off > - Timer de suspensao = Sleep timer: Off > - Velocidade da reproducao = Playback speed: Normal > - Qualidade = Quality: Auto (720p60) > > **Screenshot 2 - AdGuard OFF (dubbing works)** > > - AdGuard window: "A protecao esta desativada" = "Protection is disabled" > - YouTube player settings menu: > - Volume estavel = Stable volume: **greyed out (unavailable)** > - Iluminacao cinematografica = Ambient mode: ON > - **Faixa de audio = Audio track: Portuguese (BR)** > - Legendas/CC = Subtitles/CC: Off > - Timer de suspensao = Sleep timer: Off > - Velocidade da reproducao = Playback speed: Normal > - Qualidade = Quality: Auto (1080p60 HD) > > Note that it's not only the audio track. Stable volume also flips between the two states, which makes me think YouTube is sending a different player configuration when AdGuard is in the middle, rather than something just being hidden on the page. > > ## Environment > > - AdGuard for Windows 8.0.3 (build 8.0.5587), Windows 11 (26H2) > - Browser: Chromium-based (identifies as Chrome 156) > - Test video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZW0tKX_iFhc > - No user rules > > ## Steps to reproduce > > 1. Keep HTTPS filtering enabled (default settings). > 2. Open the test video and open the player settings (gear icon). > 3. Result: no "Audio track" option. > 4. Add `youtube.com` to Settings > HTTPS filtering > Website allowlist, restart the browser, reload the video. > 5. Result: "Audio track" is back with the dubbed languages. > 6. Remove `youtube.com` from the allowlist again: the option disappears again. > > ## Expected vs actual > > - Expected: the "Audio track" menu with dubbed languages is shown, the same as on mobile or with AdGuard off. > - Actual: with youtube.com HTTPS-filtered, the menu is missing and the player stays in the original language. > > ## What I already ruled out > > Each of these was tested on its own, and none of them brought dubbing back: > > - **DNS filters:** with only DNS protection active, dubbing works. The DNS lists (AdGuard DNS filter, YousList) don't block anything the player needs. > - **Full allowlist rule** `@@||www.youtube.com^$important,document`: still broken. > - **All JS/scriptlet rules off on YouTube** with the user rule `@@||youtube.com^$jsinject`: still broken. > - **Tracking protection (Stealth mode) fully off:** still broken. > - **Annoyances filter and AI-related filters off:** still broken. > - **AdGuard browser extension off:** no change, since the app filters the browser. > - **Other domains:** `googlevideo.com`, `ytimg.com` and `ggpht.com` don't need to be excluded. Only `youtube.com` matters. > - **Filter lists and log:** I went through the YouTube rules in the Base filter and the filtering log. Nothing touches the audio tracks, and the `/youtubei/v1/player` request isn't blocked or rewritten by any rule. > > ## Workaround and its cost > > Putting `youtube.com` in the HTTPS allowlist (or turning HTTPS filtering off) fixes dubbing, but in-video YouTube ads come back, since the app can no longer filter that traffic. > > ## Timeline > > - Until about a week ago, I could pause filtering, select the dubbed track and turn filtering back on, and it would keep working. > - About a week ago, the audio menu started showing only the original language. > - After updating to 8.0.3 (October 22, 2026), the audio menu disappeared completely and the old trick stopped working: the player falls back to the original language on reload. > > ## My guess > > Since no rule seems to be involved, I suspect the HTTPS interception itself. With AdGuard proxying the connection, YouTube sees a browser that claims to be Chrome (user agent and `x-browser-validation` header) but has AdGuard's TLS/HTTP fingerprint. YouTube may treat that as an unverified client and serve a reduced player without experimental features such as AI dubbing. > > Someone else on the same AdGuard version doesn't have this issue, so YouTube experiment groups may play a part too. > > I can send filtering log exports (with and without the exclusion) if that helps. ### Screenshots

The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The Guardian's "Disable Your Adblocker" wall could not be reproduced:⁠ the reported homepage, the exact screenshot article and two other articles loaded through the AdGuard CLI proxy baseline showed no anti-adblock markup after waiting and scrolling, and the captured requests contain no detector script that renders such a wall. Under the run instruction's anti-adblock rule this goes to a maintainer rather than getting a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The wall is not a German site's wall, and the captured request inventory contains no detector script that renders it, so the gate for writing a rule is not met. Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." The absence of the wall in this environment is an observation for a maintainer, not a decision this run may make. No rule family could be extended instead:⁠ the only site-level anti-adblock selectors already present (`.adblock-sticky__message`, `.js-adblock-sticky`) describe a different, sticky message, and the anti-adblock bait is already excepted by `theguardian.com#@#.ad_unit`.
